verdicts.why: Both fully translate the dedicatory poem and both ornament descriptions; nothing is dropped on either side.
Both render the full three paragraphs including the Precion and Salniterisch terms and the sentence-fragment ending; nothing is cut on either side.
Every title in both tables, including Zubdat al-Irfan, Al-Jawahir al-Mukallalah, and the trailing cut-off A treatise explaining, appears on both sides; no row is dropped.
Left drops the clause she said I will not see between for she said and the death of my child, while right explicitly translates it as For she said, I will not see, the death of my child.
Both sides translate the same short title-page elements, date, author, emblem description, library banner, and Hain reference, with nothing omitted.
Right wraps the opening paragraph in a <meta continues from previous page> tag but keeps all the same content ("Suns, in Gemini and Virgo"); nothing is dropped on either side.

Source is an extremely repetitive/garbled string repeating "...devoid of intrinsic nature" dozens of times; both sides condense it to the same two-sentence rendering without dropping distinct content.
Both fully translate every element (officials names, title, seal text 翰林/Hanlin); differences are naming/wording choices, not omissions.
Right drops the page header entirely, while left renders it as "Gate 20, Gate of Deaths, Chapter" from the OCR header שער כ שער שהמות פרק.
Right omits the page header translation "Preface." (OCR header Vorrede.), which left preserves as <header>Preface.</header>.
Both fully render all four letters with no dropped clauses or omitted phrases.
Right drops the explanatory notes left keeps identifying the Nuncio as The Papal Ambassador and Bembo as Pietro Bembo, the influential cardinal and scholar.
Both translate the full passage; right adds term/gloss tags for Kunst, Pfund, Mitbruedern, Finsternis, Liecht but neither omits content the other keeps.
Both render all of Surah An-Nisa verses 95-105 in full, including the fear-prayer regulations, with no dropped sentences.
Both translate the full Origen passage identically in coverage, ending at the same source cutoff (the rational governing/ruling faculty and).
Both fully render Psalm 105:8-22 plus the margin note and summary; only wording/gloss choices differ, nothing dropped.
Left drops the translated header entirely, while right opens with Preface translating the OCR header Vorrede.
Both translate the full sutra passage end-to-end with equivalent content; differences are phrasing only, nothing material is missing on either side.

Left omits the translated header and volume meta (Jingzhen Supplement, continues from Vol 27) and drops the editorial note about the possibly-typo character in the source gloss, both preserved by right.
Both render the same title, insert block, and unclear markers identically; only the summary and keyword phrasing differs.
Both sides render every marginal note, gloss, and inserted phrase; differences are in gloss wording/definitions, not dropped content.

Both fully translate the preface including the opening clause about supplying a hanging sentiment/suspended meaning and the closing colophon; right just tags it as a meta continuation instead of plain prose.
Both cover the full passage; left adds original-quote notes but the translated phrase true image of virtue is present on both sides, so nothing substantive is lost either way.
Both give a complete parallel translation of the alchemical and creation passages, including all margin notes and the closing Jubilation of the Soul or line.

Left includes two explanatory annotations right lacks: a note that the content and the one who asks references Quran 22:36, and a note on the wordplay in qawail (midday heat/afflictions), which right renders plainly with no annotation.
Both fully translate the title, shelfmark codes, and vocab; the differing meta/note additions are editorial elaboration, not source content either side drops.

Both render the full Hananiah/Zechariah ben Kabutal exchange start to finish, including the closing Because so...; differences are only in gloss-vs-note styling of terms like golah and Beit HaMikdash.
Left omits the page header entirely, while right translates it as Libri medici in Octavo -> Medical books in octavo format before entry 480.
Left's title collapses the opening line into a title without the detail that the supplication was bestowed by the face of Ugyen Rinpoche, i.e. spoken directly by him, which right keeps.
Both sides translate every fragmentary column of the commentary with no dropped clauses, only paraphrase differences.
